newsitem.title: USA: Initial jobless claims down in latest week.
newsitem.headline: Initial jobless claims down in latest week.

text.p: The number of Americans claiming first-time jobless benefits fell last week to its lowest level in nearly three months, the government said Thursday.
The Labour Department said initial jobless claims in the week ended Jan. 11 fell to 323,000 from a revised 355,000 in the previous week.
Claims in the latest week were at their lowest level since the week ended Oct. 19, when they stood at 319,000.
Wall Street economists had forecast initial jobless claims of 355,000 in the week ended Jan. 11.
The less volatile four-week moving average, which is regarded as a more accurate barometer of the labour market, fell to 348,750 last week from 355,500.
Still, the total number of Americans claiming benefits in the same week swelled to its highest level in nearly a year.

Continued claims for the week ended Jan. 4, the latest period for which data were available, rose to 2.71 million, the highest since the week ended Feb. 3, 1996, when they reached nearly 2.76 million.
The department said 17 states and one territory reported decreases in claims exceeding 1,000 on an unadjusted basis in the week ended Jan. 4, the latest period for which data were available.
Among the largest were Wisconsin, with 12,094; Michigan, with 10,137; Kentucky, with 8,746; Illinois, with 8,713; Massachusetts, with 7,676; and Iowa, with 7,108.
Wisconsin reported fewer layoffs in manufacturing and the construction, trade and service industries, while Michigan reported fewer layoffs in various industries throughout the state.

Kentucky had fewer layoffs in the electrical equipment, rubber and primary metals industries and Illinois had fewer layoffs in the construction and service industries and in manufacturing. Massachusetts and Iowa provided no explanation.
The department said 11 states reported increases in initial claims exceeding 1,000, unadjusted, in the Jan. 4 week.
Among the largest were North Carolina, with 27,879; New York, with 19,998; South Carolina, with 12,355; Alabama, with 10,049; and California, with 6,175.

North Carolina reported layoffs in the construction, service, textile, apparel, furniture, lumber, rubber and glass industries and manufucturing. New York had layoffs in the construction and service industries, as well as holiday shutdowns in various industries.
South Carolina reported layoffs in the textile industry, while Alabama said there were layoffs in the textile, apparel and lumber industries and in manufacturing.
California had layoffs in the construction, trade, service and transportation industries. It also reported layoffs in agriculture, as well as holiday shutdowns in various industries.
